I recommend closing Plant 6 and moving its product family to the other plants.

Closing also has the lowest one-time cost, $10.0 million for moving equipment and closing the site. Retooling needs $30.0 million up front, and selling gives only $37.5 million in proceeds while losing income every year. Closing is the only option that improves the Company's results from the first year. Every option can be paid from the $444.9 million of liquidity, so the choice rests on the operating income effect.

Closing keeps the product family's revenue, since the other plants have room for about $361.0 million of added revenue. The plant's cost above the Company's average is roughly halved when production moves.

For the workforce, I have offered positions at the other plants to 29 employees, the most the Company's expected acceptance rate allows at about 15% of those offered. Those who accept receive $20,000 each in relocation help. The remaining 161 roles are eliminated, with severance of about $4,566 per person, roughly $0.7 million in total. The other plants need 190 positions for the moved products. Staff who do not relocate are replaced by hiring near the other plants, so the Company's production capacity is maintained.

The cost of this allocation is severance of about $0.7 million and relocation of about $0.6 million, both one-time. The annual benefit of $16.5 million outweighs these costs within the first year. The Company should also tell the affected communities and employees early, and support those who leave with outplacement help.

I recommend closing Plant 6 and moving its product family to the other plants. Of the options, closing produces the largest improvement in the Company's operating income: about $16.5 million a year, compared with $7.5 million a year from retooling and a $15.3 million a year reduction from selling. Its one-time cost of $10.0 million is small against liquidity of $444.9 million, and the Company keeps the product family's $361.0 million of revenue, which the other plants have room to absorb.

Plant 6's operating result is -$9.0 million only after $32.4 million of allocated corporate costs. Those costs stay with the Company under every option, so the plant's real contribution is the $23.4 million it earns before them, but the cost structure above the Company's average, about $32.9 million a year, is what closing removes. Half of it is recovered by moving production to plants with more volume.

Employees: the other plants need 190 positions for the moved products, so Plant 6 workers are the natural first source. Management expects about 15% of those offered to accept, capped at 29 people, so I have assigned 29 to positions at the other plants, with relocation support of $20,000 each. The remaining 161 roles are eliminated, with severance of about $4,566 per person on average. Sale and retooling would have left a larger number of people without a role under the current options, and neither offers a better outcome for operating income.

Risks: the 50% cost recovery and the relocation take-up are management estimates, and the other plants must absorb the workload on schedule. I recommend monitoring acceptance of the 29 positions and the transfer timing closely, and reviewing the outcome against the $16.5 million target after the first full year.
